title: Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – Native Soil Inc. – Manzanita Elementary School Upper Yard Site Improvement Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and Native Soil Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to demolish existing play structures, safety surfacing, basketball hoop poles, and remove existing planter boxes, mulch, and retaining wall adjacent to play structures; install safety surfacing tiles and drainage systems; (New play structure to be installed by others.); perform additional work including preparing walls for murals, tree planting with irrigation and drainage, upgrade to the nature area, and pavement replacement; and as further described in the Bid Form Document 00 31 01, incorporated herein by reference as though fully set forth, for the Manzanita Elementary School Upper Yard Site Improvement Project, in the amount of $430,815.00, which includes a contingency allowance of $53,000.00, as the lowest responsible bidder, rejecting all other bids, if any, with the work anticipated to commence on August 25, 2025, and required to be completed within sixty (60) days, with an anticipated ending of October 24, 2025.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Hires Native Soil for $430,815 to replace play structures and surfacing at Manzanita Elementary
summary: Native Soil Inc. would tear out old play structures, safety surfacing and planter boxes in the upper yard at Manzanita Elementary, then install new safety surfacing and drainage. Extra work includes tree planting, a nature area upgrade, new pavement and preparing walls for murals. The price includes a $53,000 cushion for contingencies. Native Soil was the lowest responsible bidder, with work expected from August 25 to October 24, 2025. The new play structure will be installed by others.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Nonpublic, Nonsectarian School, Agency Services Master Contract 2025-26 - Intermountain Deaconess Children’s Services - Special Education Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Nonpublic, Nonsectarian School/ Agency Services Master Contract 2025-26 by and between the District and Intermountain Deaconess Children’s Services, Helena, MT, for the latter to provide Special Education services, stated in Agreement, required by a student’s Individualized Education Program, for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, via the Special Education Department, in an amount not to exceed $800,000.00.
headline: Pays Intermountain Deaconess Children’s Services up to $800,000 for special education services in 2025-26

title: Lease Agreement - Marion Fong - Real Property for Staff and Visitor Parking - Lincoln Elementary School

official_text: Adoption by the Board of Education, upon recommendation by the Measures N and H Commission, of a 2025-2026 Education Improvement Plan/Budget modification for Young Adult Program to reduce $5,065.50 Meeting Refreshments by $4,536.12 to $529.38 and adding or transferring the $4,536.12  to $81,209.50, increasing to $85,745.62 funding for Teacher on Special Assignment, School, as stated in the justification section of the New or Revised Strategic Action Section of the Budget Modification Form.

headline: Moves $4,536.12 from meeting refreshments to a teacher position in the Young Adult Program

title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement – Terraphase Engineering Inc. – Garfield Elementary School Modernization Project - Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement by and between the District and Terraphase Engineering Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide a traffic and circulation analysis to address transportation-related issues identified in the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) checklist, for the Garfield Elementary School Modernization Project, in an additional amount of $17,545.00, which includes a contingency fee of $1,595.00, increasing the Agreement’s not-to-exceed amount from $81,381.00 to $98,926.00, and extending the term of the Agreement from May 15, 2025 through December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026, (an additional 181 calendar days).  All other terms and conditions of the Agreement remain in full force and effect.
presenter: Deputy Chief, Facilities Planning and Management
headline: Adds $17,545 and more time for Terraphase's traffic study for Garfield Elementary
summary: Terraphase Engineering is doing a traffic and circulation analysis for the Garfield Elementary School Modernization Project, to address issues raised in the environmental review. title: Graydon Exception to Public Bidding - Microsoft Volume Licensing Agreement, Enrollment - Softchoice, Inc. - Technology Services Department

title: Construction Agreement Between Owner and Contractor – D-Line Constructors, Inc. – Montera Middle School Site Improvements Project – Division of Facilities Planning and Management
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of the Construction Agreement Between Owner and Contractor by and between the District and D-Line Constructors, Inc., Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide “construction services to provide seal coating approximately 43,672.45 square feet of the lower yard area, with crack sealing performed as needed. title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Student Assignment Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide coordination and administrative support to improve family engagement and satisfaction during District’s peak enrollment season by facilitating clerical, technical, and student-led media engagement activities; support the Digital Ambassador Program, a component of BP 5115 that highlights District schools through short social media clips and school-based storytelling; provide stipends and mentorship for District students who assist in producing promotional audio-visual content that showcases school programs, culture, and community partnerships; coordinate and support  enrollment work in selected, peak periods; collaborate with the Student Assignment Center to streamline enrollment processes and increase school visibility-helping to boost and stabilize enrollment district-wide; reduce the number of families who do not respond to initial offers by ten percent, and increase family satisfaction ratings on Zendesk by five percentage points, via Student Assignment Department, for the period of November 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $72,050.00.
headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $72,050 to support enrollment season outreach
summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund will help the Student Assignment Department during the peak enrollment season. Its work includes a student-led social media program that showcases schools, stipends and mentorship for the students who make the videos, and support for enrollment work. The goals are to cut the number of families who do not respond to first offers by ten percent and raise family satisfaction ratings by five percentage points. The term runs from November 1, 2025 to July 31, 2026.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - A-Tech Consulting - Risk Management Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and A-Tech Consulting, Orange, CA, for the latter, in accordance with U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) 3Ts Program (Training, Testing, and Taking Action voluntary program) for Reducing Lead in Drinking Water guidelines, as well as District internal standards, provide: 1) Sampling Coverage-Conduct sequential sampling at each site for every: a) Drinking water fountain; b) Filtered water stations; c) Kitchen preparation sink; d) Kitchen three-compartment sink; 2) Sampling & Laboratory Analysis: a) Collect samples following EPA 3Ts protocols for sequential lead testing (e.g., 125-125-250 mL sequence for fountains; 250 mL for filtered water stations); b) Maintain full chain of custody (CoC) for each sample; c) Submit samples to an EPA-certified laboratory for analysis; d) Laboratory analysis costs shall be billed per sample; 3) Logistics & Reporting: a) Clearly label and document all sampled fixtures; b) Process CoC documentation accurately and promptly; c) Provide consolidated, site-specific laboratory reports with results compared against EPA and OUSD action levels;4) Staffing & Timeline: a) Assign sufficient staff and authorize overtime as needed to meet testing and processing demands; b) Expedite analysis to ensure all results are available before the start of the new school year, via Risk Management Department, for the period of July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $50,000.00.
headline: Ratifies up to $50,000 for A-Tech Consulting to test school drinking water for lead
summary: A-Tech Consulting will collect and lab-test water samples for lead at district sites, following the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) 3Ts program. headline: Pays Ignite The Mind up to $75,000 for group tutoring and mentoring at McClymonds High
summary: Ignite The Mind runs group tutoring and mentorship for about 150 to 200 students, focused on seniors, English Language Learners and students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) or 504 Plans. Each student gets two sessions a week. The contract runs January 1, 2026 through May 31, 2026, and the Board is approving it after the work began.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - Oakland Public Education Fund - McClymonds High School
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund (OPEF), Oakland, CA, for the latter to manage the stipend process for student mentors from McClymonds High School and student mentees from Westlake Middle School participating in the Cross-Age Mentoring Program (CAMP), including setting up McClymonds High School student mentors and their mentees at West Oakland Middle School with a stipend process and timeline, issuing stipend payments to McClymonds High School lead staff who will disperse stipends to student mentors and their mentees, along with issuing year-end tax documents to stipend recipients, via McClymonds High School, for the period of January 1, 2026, through May 31, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $44,000.00.
headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $44,000 to run student mentor stipend payments

headline: Moves $100 within Oakland High's college and career funds to cover Sacramento and LA trip lodging

headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $150,000 to employ summer program and youth coaching staff
summary: Oakland Public Education Fund will serve as fiscal agent, meaning it employs and pays staff, for OUSD summer programs. These include two four-week June arts camps at Oakland Performing Arts and the Roosevelt Summer Music Program, serving up to 150 students daily, and eight community-based youth development coaches supporting over 4,000 students across 40 campuses. The agreement runs May 18 through June 30, 2026.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: No Cost Services Agreement - 2025-2026 - No-Cost - Students Rising Above - Oakland High School
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a No Cost Services Agreement - 2025-2026 by and between the District and Students Rising Above, San Francisco, CA, for the latter to support and oversee the transition of the UC Berkeley, Education Talent Search (ETS) TRIO program, which has identified and served Oakland High School (OHS) seniors, with College Advisors, providing a targeted senior cohort with small group advising focused on college applications, college enrollment, FAFSA, and CA Dream Act completion, Scholarship applications, transition planning, along with individualized academic advising by assisting in meeting with seniors on University of C and California State University college entrance requirements at Oakland High School for the period of November 1, 2025 through May 31, 2026, at no cost to the District.
headline: Approves a no-cost deal for Students Rising Above to give Oakland High seniors college advising
summary: Students Rising Above of San Francisco will take over from the UC Berkeley Education Talent Search (ETS) TRIO program, providing college advisors to Oakland High School seniors. Advising covers college applications and enrollment, financial aid forms, scholarships and transition planning, plus help meeting University of California and California State University entrance requirements. It runs November 1, 2025 through May 31, 2026 at no cost to the district. The board is approving it after the start date.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

official_text:
Ratification by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and Aaron Bray, Los Angeles, CA, for the latter to provide four 2-hour training courses for up to 100 participants:

Session 1 Description - This interactive workshop will allow participants to apply transformative justice practices to a scenario where a group of students are bullying another student on Instagram. .

title: Services Agreement 2025-2026 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Services Agreement 2025-2026 by and between the District and Oakland Public Education Fund, Oakland, CA, for the latter to provide comprehensive housing navigation services three days per week on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays from eight thirty in the morning until four in the afternoon at 746 Grand Avenue in Oakland, including conducting crisis intake and triage, verifying McKinney-Vento eligibility, and providing immediate enrollment and transportation support for students to maintain educational stability at their school of origin; facilitate emergency shelter placements and connect families to the Coordinated Entry System while providing tenant-landlord advocacy to prevent eviction for at least fifteen families; provide financial literacy coaching and budgeting education to all sixty families and link at least forty-five families to two or more external support resources such as CalFresh or Medi-Cal to promote long-term self-sufficiency, for a total of twenty-two and a half hours of weekly service over the contract term; and ensure that seventy percent of students in participating families maintain consistent enrollment in their school of origin and achieve a ten percent reduction in chronic absenteeism rates, via Community Schools and Student Services Department, for the period of March 2, 2026 through June 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00.
headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $10,000 for housing help for families in need
summary: The Oakland Public Education Fund would provide housing navigation services three days a week at 746 Grand Avenue. Services include crisis intake, checking eligibility under the McKinney-Vento Act (the federal law protecting students experiencing homelessness), school enrollment and transportation help, shelter placement and help avoiding eviction. The goal is to serve 60 families from March 2 to June 30, 2026, for up to $10,000, and the period began before board approval.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement (MOU or Agreement) for an Intern Partnership Program and Practica Program-applying to credentials in TK-12 Teaching, including Multiple Subjects, Single Subjects, Designated Subjects, and Special Education Categories, including Added or Supplementary Authorizations; including Pupil Personnel Services in Communicative Sciences & Disorders, Mental Health & Wellness, Counseling & Guidance, Education Intervention or Educational Therapy, Social Work, Administration, and other Pupil Personnel Services credentials and certifications, as may be specified; including Fieldwork Experience for Master of Arts or Science and other Graduate-Level Degrees or Certifications with Emphasis in Pupil Personnel Services; including Fieldwork Experience for Pre-Credential Candidate Undergraduate Students-is entered into by and between Oakland Unified School District (District or OUSD), a public school district in the State of California, County of Alameda, and Dominican University of California (University or DU), a California nonprofit, private university in San Rafael, County of Marin-for the term July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031 at no cost to the District other than for certain Non-Teaching Interns in PPS categories (Article 6/#6), who are not employees of the District but may be allocated stipends (Article 6/#6) drawn from non-profit organizational grants to the District (e.g. Ed Fund), administered by the relevant departments of the District. headline: Creates a five-year, mostly no-cost intern partnership with Dominican University
summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) and interagency agreement sets up an intern and practicum program with Dominican University of California for teaching credentials and pupil personnel services such as counseling, social work and speech-language fields. outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement – Waste Management of Alameda County, Inc. – Solid Waste Handling & Recycling Services Project – Custodial Services Department
official_text:
Approval by the Board of Education of Amendment No. 1, General Services Agreement by and between the District and Waste Management of Alameda County, Inc., for the latter to provide solid waste handling, recycling, and composting services for the Solid Waste Handling & Recycling Services Project,
·	in the amount of $3,675,000.00, for the term August 13, 2025, through June 30, 2026;

headline: Extends Waste Management's trash, recycling and compost service through June 2028, up to $12.24M total
summary: Waste Management of Alameda County handles trash, recycling and composting for the district. This amendment keeps current rates for July 2026 through June 2027 (up to $4,200,000 that year) and allows up to a 4% rate increase for July 2027 through June 2028 (up to $4,368,000). Counting the $3,675,000 for the first term that began August 13, 2025, the total can reach $12,243,000.
vendor_name: Waste Management of Alameda County, Inc.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - District and Trustees of the California State University, on behalf of California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement (MOU or Agreement) for an Intern Partnership Program and Practica Program applying to credentials in TK-12 Teaching, including Multiple Subjects, Single Subjects, Designated Subjects, and Special Education Categories, including Added or Supplementary Authorizations; including Pupil Personnel Services in Communicative Sciences & Disorders, Mental Health & Wellness, Counseling & Guidance, Education Intervention or Educational Therapy, Social Work, Administration, and other Pupil Personnel Services credentials and certifications, as may be specified; including Fieldwork Experience for Master of Arts or Science and other Graduate-Level Degrees or Certifications with Emphasis in Pupil Personnel Services; including Fieldwork Experience for Pre-Credential Candidate Undergraduate Students-is entered into by and between Oakland Unified School District (District or OUSD), a public school district in the State of California, County of Alameda, and the Trustees of California State University, on behalf of the California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (University or CSPUH), a California State University-for the term July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031 at no cost to the District other than for certain Non-Teaching Interns in PPS categories (Article 6/#6), who are not employees of the District but may be allocated stipends (Article 6/#6) drawn from non-profit organizational grants to the District (e.g. Ed Fund), administered by the relevant departments of the District. [See Fiscal Impact]
headline: Five-year, no-cost partnership with Cal Poly Humboldt to host teacher and student-support interns

It runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031. It costs the district nothing, except that some non-teaching interns in student-support fields may receive stipends paid from nonprofit grants to the district, such as from the Ed Fund.
vendor_name: Trustees of the California State University, on behalf of California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

headline: Hires a speech-language pathologist for up to $114,000 to serve students in special education
summary: Rachel Hart of San Leandro will work as a school-based speech and language pathologist for students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs, their legal special education plans). Her duties include speech and language services, assessments, IEP meetings, progress reports, Medi-Cal billing, case management and communication with families and staff. The contract runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and is capped at $114,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Service Agreement 2025-2026 - Jacobson Education Law - Special Education Department

title: Service Agreement - Michelle Falise - Special Education Department

(CA License No. OC36861), covering All Enrolled Students While:

• On school campus grounds during regular school days and hours, including, whilst continuously on campus grounds, the hour immediately before and after scheduled classes.

• Participating in school-affiliated and supervised activities, including interscholastic athletics (excluding tackle football), off-season athletic training and conditioning, approved/sponsored work study, junior military programs, and field trip programs within the United States that remain under the control of school staff and/or designated adult chaperones.

headline: Pays Alliant Insurance $72,707.65 for 2026-27 accident insurance covering all enrolled students
summary: This insurance covers accidental injuries to all enrolled students while on campus during school hours, during supervised school activities such as sports (except tackle football) and field trips, and while traveling directly between home and school. title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - Smith College - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement (MOU or Agreement) for a Practicum Learning Experience Program-applying to District placements of College students, regarding course work for Advanced Degrees and Certifications, including the field of Social Work, and including Master of Arts or Science and other Graduate-Level Degrees or Certifications with Emphasis in Pupil Personnel Services, and other Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) credentials and certifications, as may be specified-is entered into by and between OAKLAND UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT (District or OUSD), a public school district in the state of California, County of Alameda, and Smith College (SC or College), on behalf of its School For Social Work (SCSSW), an independent, nonprofit private college in Northampton, Massachusetts-for the term July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031, at no cost to the District, other than for certain Non-Teaching Interns in PPS categories (Article 4/#2), who are not employees of the District but may be allocated stipends (Article 4/#3) drawn from non-profit organizational grants to the District (e.g. Ed Fund), administered by the relevant departments of the District. title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - Board of Trustees of Stanford University - Stanford Graduate School of Education - Research, Assessment, and Data (RAD) Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a No Cost Services Agreement (NCSA) and a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA), both, by and between the District and the Board of Trustees of Stanford University, on behalf f its Stanford Graduate School of Education, Stanford, CA, for the latter, under the NCSA, to partner with OUSD teachers to provide support for teachers' own goals though co-planning sessions and grow of their practice through thought partnership w/ researchers and other participants; provide OUSD with aggregated and de-identified information about multilingual learner math language practices which will be integrated into classrooms based on the participating teachers' goals; and facilitate OUSD to gain access to open-source tools built on the project to assess student math talk, for the period of January 30, 2026 through December 31, 2026, and under the DSA defining the terms and conditions of the District's transmission of or sharing of pupil data with the Board of Trustees of Stanford University, or its agent, and the protection by the Board of Trustees of Stanford University, or its agent, of such data, pursuant to the terms and conditions stated in the DSA, via, the Department of Secondary Instruction and the Research and Assessment Department (RAD), for the same term as specified in the NCSA, each Agreement, at no cost to the District.
headline: Ratifies a no-cost research partnership with Stanford to support teachers' math language practices
summary: The board is approving a no-cost services agreement with Stanford Graduate School of Education. Researchers will work with OUSD teachers on co-planning to support multilingual learners' math talk, share de-identified results and offer open-source tools. A data sharing agreement (DSA) sets rules for sharing and protecting student data. Both run January 30 through December 31, 2026, at no cost to the district.
vendor_name: Board of Trustees of Stanford University (Stanford Graduate School of Education)
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding - Alameda Health System - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text:
Ratification by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) by and between the District and Alameda Health System (AHS), to help meet the medical health, mental health education and youth development needs of students, and through partnering with other services providers on campuses to provide a holistic set of wrap-around services that remove barriers to learning and ensure increase access to care, through school-based health centers, the latter will provide the following services: 
1. 	Dental screening and treatment
2. 	Health education for students and families
3. 	Outreach to youth and their families
4. 	Community-wide health promotion events and activities
5. 	Student referrals for services (at Frick Academy Wellness Center and alternate community clinics or community programs)
at no cost to the District, students, or parents unless provided otherwise by this MOU, for the period August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, via the Community Schools and Student Services Department.
headline: Ratifies a no-cost agreement with Alameda Health System for school-based health services
summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) has Alameda Health System offer services through school-based health centers: dental screening and treatment, health education for students and families, outreach, community health events, and referrals for care. The services are at no cost to the district, students or parents unless the MOU says otherwise. It covers August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

summary: Children Rising will provide a coordinator to enroll families in its math and reading tutoring, update parents on their child's progress, and host monthly Zoom coaching sessions on learning strategies for home. outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
